To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have cloned a nearly full-length cDNA of a bovine liver ACT protease inhibitor that possesses a high degree (55%) of homology with human ACT and contains a predicted P1 serine at the reactive site, which is consistent with the hypothesis of multiple isoforms of bovin ACT.
bovine liver alpha 1- antichymotrysin (ACT) contains multiple isoforms, which vary in reactive-site residues.
the bovine ACT protease inhibitor gene encodes multiple isoforms of ACT, which vary in reactive-site residues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular cloning, characterization, and expression of bovine ACT, and it provides a molecular basis for the comparison of the protease inhibitor in cattle with that in man.
the molecular cloning and characterization of ACTs from bovine liver and provides the first report of ACT isoforms in a mammalian species.
the molecular cloning of ACT isoforms in bovine and the demonstration of heterogeneity in the P1 residue of ACTs in bovine liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bovine alpha-1-antichemotrypsin is not a single protein, but rather a family of proteins.
the P1 position (the NH2-terminal side residue) of the cleaved scissile peptide bond of bovine ACT is serine, and the P1 position in human ACT is leucine.
ACTs from different species vary in the reactive site and, therefore, in the protease specificity of the reactive-site peptide bond.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bovine ACT cDNAs and genes are similar to human ACT cDNAs in that they are expressed in the liver, but they differ from human ACT in that they are heterogeneous and possess multiple P1 residues.
bovine ACT is encoded by multiple genes, and that the P1 residue of the reactive site varies among isoforms.
the bovine ACT cDNAs encode ACTs with different P1 residues in the reactive site and that the P1 residue may play a significant role in the specificity of bovine ACTs toward various proteases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bovine ACT is a heterogenous protease inhibitor that contains isoforms with distinct P1 residues.
bovine alpha 2-macroglobulin is a protease inhibitor with high homology to human alpha 2-macro-globulin.
the bovine ACT cDNAs we cloned are the first to be identified from the bovine liver, and the first to reveal the heterogeneity in P 1 residues of the reactive site in ACT.
